separation_rule: A claim definition, current evidence, proof decision, and downstream ceiling are independent; evidence existence never promotes a claim by itself.

claims.name: Canonical source contract
claims.expected_behavior: The live adopted contract, source tree, semantic inventories, and generated projections resolve to one authority with no missing, duplicate, stale, or circular reference.
claims.truth_surface: live canonical source tree and adopted contract
claims.claim_guard: Source coherence proves no package or runtime behavior.
claims.repair: Resolve the canonical owner, repair or regenerate affected authority, invalidate dependent evidence, and independently revalidate the live tree.
claims.rerun: Recompute LiveContext and candidate identity, invalidate stale dependent evidence, then rerun strict proof for CL-SOURCE with the named independent reconciler.

claims.name: Built package identity
claims.expected_behavior: The built package contains exactly the intended product components and can be reproduced or honestly bounded at every non-reproducible dimension.
claims.truth_surface: built package bytes and generated package inventory
required_evidence: clean build inputs and toolchain identity
claims.claim_guard: Package identity proves no install or discovery.
claims.repair: Correct package generation or inventory ownership, rebuild from a clean context, and repeat independent unpack/reinventory and reproducibility checks.
claims.rerun: Recompute LiveContext and candidate identity, invalidate stale dependent evidence, then rerun strict proof for CL-PACKAGE with the named independent reconciler.

claims.name: Installed bytes
claims.expected_behavior: The exact verified package bytes are installed only into the authorized target with observable identity, bounded effects, and a tested recovery path.
claims.truth_surface: measured installed bytes in authorized target
claims.claim_guard: Installed bytes prove no host discovery.
claims.repair: Remove or quarantine the incorrect installation without losing user work, install the intended bytes into the authorized target, and rerun byte reconciliation.
claims.rerun: Recompute LiveContext and candidate identity, invalidate stale dependent evidence, then rerun strict proof for CL-INSTALL with the named independent reconciler.

claims.name: Host discovery
claims.expected_behavior: A supported host discovers the intended installed plugin identity in a newly loaded session through the documented marketplace/discovery route.
claims.truth_surface: supported host's exposed discovery observation in a new session
claims.claim_guard: Discovery proves no representative route behavior.
claims.repair: Repair marketplace or manifest wiring, remove or disambiguate stale versions under authority, reload the host, and repeat the independent discovery probe.
claims.rerun: Recompute LiveContext and candidate identity, invalidate stale dependent evidence, then rerun strict proof for CL-DISCOVERY with the named independent reconciler.

claims.name: Representative runtime behavior
claims.expected_behavior: The discovered plugin front door, canonical skills, supported custom agents, and CLI kernel perform representative product-semantic actions with the declared effects and identity.
claims.truth_surface: representative live plugin and CLI invocations
false_pass_controls: direct binary invocation that bypasses plugin
single happy-path command treated as product proof
claims.claim_guard: One invocation proves only the exercised behavior and environment.
claims.repair: Repair the failing route or capability degradation behavior, reload the actual installed product, and rerun the exact representative journey under a fresh context.
claims.rerun: Recompute LiveContext and candidate identity, invalidate stale dependent evidence, then rerun strict proof for CL-RUNTIME with the named independent reconciler.

claims.name: Repository fitting behavior
claims.expected_behavior: Fresh setup and existing-repository retrofit inspect, plan, apply, and verify bounded repository changes while preserving user authority and producing usable loaded behavior.
false_pass_controls: files present but host ignores them
claims.claim_guard: Generated files or receipts do not prove loaded behavior or preservation.
claims.repair: Reconcile ownership/conflicts, restore user work where needed, revise the fit plan, apply only authorized mutations, and repeat post-fit behavior verification.
claims.rerun: Recompute LiveContext and candidate identity, invalidate stale dependent evidence, then rerun strict proof for CL-FIT with the named independent reconciler.

claims.name: Routine development behavior
claims.expected_behavior: Routine work remains fast and useful on a dirty tree by selecting a legally dependency-closed affected set, verifying reuse, preserving local work, and reporting actual execution.
claims.truth_surface: dirty-tree affected-set execution and preserved workspace
claims.claim_guard: A green subset is valid only if impact closure and reuse are verified.
claims.repair: Invalidate unsafe reuse, expand the affected closure, restore unexpected mutations, and rerun only the corrected dependency-closed routine profile.
claims.rerun: Recompute LiveContext and candidate identity, invalidate stale dependent evidence, then rerun strict proof for CL-ROUTINE with the named independent reconciler.

claims.name: Observability behavior
claims.expected_behavior: Local semantic events can be queried to explain cause and repair without hidden query writes; any adopted external export is explicit, privacy-bounded, and roundtrip-verified.
claims.truth_surface: local query behavior and optional export roundtrip
required_evidence: explicit export effect and collector reconciliation when adopted
false_pass_controls: event existence used as behavior proof
claims.claim_guard: Event presence cannot prove product behavior or claims.
claims.repair: Correct event semantics, storage/query purity, privacy controls, or export reconciliation; purge unsafe data under authority and rerun the affected observation path.
claims.rerun: Recompute LiveContext and candidate identity, invalidate stale dependent evidence, then rerun strict proof for CL-OBSERVABILITY with the named independent reconciler.

claims.name: Strict validation profile
claims.expected_behavior: Strict proof selects one named claim, closes its exact dependency boundary, executes positive and adversarial controls, binds evidence to the live candidate, and obtains independent reconciliation.
claims.truth_surface: claim-specific dependency-closed proof with negative controls
claims.claim_guard: Receipts/tests/rows cannot substitute for named behavior.
claims.repair: Reject the invalid evidence, repair the behavior or proof adapter, recompute the live claim boundary, and rerun with an independent reconciler.
claims.rerun: Recompute LiveContext and candidate identity, invalidate stale dependent evidence, then rerun strict proof for CL-STRICT with the named independent reconciler.

claims.name: Adaptive orchestration behavior
claims.expected_behavior: The Ultra root decomposes live dependency-ready work, grants disjoint leases, confines workers, independently reviews outputs, and alone reconciles shared authority and integration.
claims.truth_surface: live work graph, leases, worker outputs, reviews, and root reconciliation
claims.claim_guard: Parallel activity or merged code alone does not prove safe orchestration.
claims.repair: Revoke conflicting leases, preserve work, recompute state, isolate or replay affected changes, and have the root reconcile only independently accepted outputs.
claims.rerun: Recompute LiveContext and candidate identity, invalidate stale dependent evidence, then rerun strict proof for CL-ORCHESTRATION with the named independent reconciler.

claims.name: Evaluation and improvement behavior
claims.expected_behavior: Evaluations use valid representative tasks and scorers, expose artifacts and configuration, resist contamination/reward hacking, and promote only independently reviewed behavior improvements.
claims.truth_surface: audited tasks/scorers, paired runs, guarded non-regression, and review
false_pass_controls: prompt text used as runtime metadata
claims.claim_guard: Metric gain alone does not prove product improvement.
claims.repair: Repair or reject invalid tasks/scorers, rerun a representative paired evaluation, inspect artifacts, and withhold promotion until independent non-regression review passes.
claims.rerun: Recompute LiveContext and candidate identity, invalidate stale dependent evidence, then rerun strict proof for CL-EVAL-IMPROVEMENT with the named independent reconciler.

claims.name: Representative product journeys
claims.expected_behavior: Fresh users, agents, and maintainers can acquire, enter, fit, use, diagnose, observe, improve, and upgrade the product without hidden expert context or proof-shaped shortcuts.
claims.truth_surface: fresh user/agent and maintainer journeys in supported environments
false_pass_controls: artifact presence in place of use
claims.claim_guard: Artifact presence or internal tests do not prove quality in use.
claims.repair: Repair routing, language, automation, failure diagnosis, or supported-environment behavior and repeat the journey with a genuinely fresh independent actor.
claims.rerun: Recompute LiveContext and candidate identity, invalidate stale dependent evidence, then rerun strict proof for CL-REAL-JOURNEY with the named independent reconciler.

claims.name: Release readiness
claims.expected_behavior: A specific live release candidate satisfies the exact adopted release proof set across source, package, install, discovery, runtime, journeys, migration, security, and supply boundaries.
claims.truth_surface: exact live release proof set, verified package, supported install/discovery, and resolved release decisions
required_evidence: candidate identity and clean release baseline
claims.independent_reconciler: independent release reviewer and human release authority
claims.claim_guard: Release candidate is not integrated product completion.
claims.repair: Resolve the exact failed prerequisite or external decision, rebuild/rebind the candidate as needed, invalidate stale evidence, and rerun the complete release proof set.
claims.rerun: Recompute LiveContext and candidate identity, invalidate stale dependent evidence, then rerun strict proof for CL-RELEASE with the named independent reconciler.

claims.name: Integrated goal completion
claims.expected_behavior: The live integrated product closes every mandatory law, requirement, surface, custom tool, product journey, material finding, retirement obligation, and required decision at its exact claim boundary.
claims.truth_surface: root-reconciled closure of all required live claims, surfaces, tools, journeys, findings, and decisions
required_evidence: resolved material findings and required decisions
claims.independent_reconciler: Ultra root plus independent final reviewers
false_pass_controls: hidden external blocker or unsupported environment
claims.claim_guard: Goal state, green finalizer, telemetry, package, or report cannot substitute for integrated completion.
claims.repair: Keep the goal incomplete, report the highest honest ceiling, repair or obtain authority for the exact blocker, recompute all affected live state, and rerun dependent claims only.
claims.rerun: Recompute LiveContext and candidate identity, invalidate stale dependent evidence, then rerun strict proof for CL-COMPLETION with the named independent reconciler.
